findings.text: follow-on: the cutover PID coercion restored here (coerce_pid=True, fleet_migrate.py:132-136, called from _local_session_processes at fleet_migrate.py:456) has no test — neither local-reader test writes a numeric pid as a string (test_fleet_migrate_cutover.py:259 and test_fleet_migrate.py:260 both use an integer pid). The capability was silently dropped by 42c2ad36 and only restored by 8bd17f310, which is itself the proof that nothing covers it: a record with "pid": "4321" now matches again, but a future reader refactor can drop it a second time with the suite green.

follow-on: test_the_follow_loop_sweeps_on_a_cadence_not_every_iteration is a monitor of the machine rather than a unit test — _follow_watch_lines reaches _check_consumer, which calls runs.follower_owner() and reads the RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER environment variable (runs.py:2956) for an owner pid it then probes for liveness; nothing in this test injects that owner, so the loop ends after one pass when the stamped pid is dead (one sweep, not the three asserted). It fails deterministically in a session whose RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER names a finished process and passes when the variable is unset, so the gate result is a function of the reviewing session's environment, not of the code.
